threads.body: The URL-controlled `ref` is passed directly into `provision`, where it becomes part of `cache_dir() / f"{label}-{ref}"`; values containing `..` (and backslashes on Windows) can therefore make the extraction target escape the cache, and an existing target is recursively deleted before replacement. Derive the cache component from a filesystem-safe encoding or digest of the repo/ref rather than interpolating the raw ref.

Resolve/localize the effective package registry (package declaration first, caller default second) before invoking `_coverage`.

This pattern identifies any string ending in `.git` as a URL, including valid local paths such as `../registry.git`. Those paths previously worked, but now bypass CLI absolutization and `local_registry` raises the GitHub-only error. Require a URL scheme before classifying the value as a git URL so local `.git` directories remain paths.

This issue also appears on line 105 of the same file.

+    r"(?:\[(?P<sub_folder>[^\]]+)\])?$"
+)

threads.body:
The URL group is greedy, so a valid declaration such as `https://github.com/org/repo.git@release.git` captures the entire string as `url` and leaves `ref` unset. `_local_registry` then derives the nonexistent repository `org/repo.git@release` and fetches `HEAD`. Make the URL portion reluctant (or otherwise split at the first `.git@`) so refs ending in `.git` are preserved.

threads.body: Refs from the new URL syntax are accepted with `/` (for example, `@release/v1`) and passed through to `provision`, which interpolates them unescaped into `/archive/{ref}.tar.gz`. GitHub requires slashes in a branch/tag name to be percent-encoded; otherwise they become extra URL path segments and the fetch fails. Percent-encode the ref (for example with `quote(ref, safe="")`) when constructing the archive URL.
